text: {"question":"How does adding high‑redshift observations such as BAO and CMB change the sensitivity of the baryon density parameter to the Hubble constant compared with a low‑redshift analysis, and what does this suggest about the ability of evolving dark‑energy models to address the Hubble tension?","reference_answer":"When BAO and CMB data are included, the baryon density becomes tightly constrained and strongly anti‑correlated with the Hubble constant (r≈−0.97), whereas in a low‑redshift fit it is essentially uncorrelated with H0. This shift indicates that high‑redshift probes provide the leverage needed to test whether evolving dark‑energy scenarios can reconcile the low H0 values preferred by DESI BAO data with the higher values from early‑time measurements."}
